name: ADU vs Room Addition: Long-Term ROI in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: How do I compare the long-term ROI of building a detached ADU versus doing a large room addition in Los Angeles County?
mainEntity.text: How do I compare the long-term ROI of building a detached ADU versus doing a large room addition in Los Angeles County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Homeowners often ask whether to build a detached ADU or expand their main home, but most online advice only compares upfront cost, not long-term return. A better comparison in Los Angeles County starts with basic numbers: total project cost, added square footage, and how that space will be used. For a detached ADU, consider potential rental income based on realistic neighborhood rents, expected vacancy, and management effort. Factor in how the ADU will affect property taxes and insurance, as well as added utilities and maintenance. The upside is ongoing cash flow, flexibility for family housing, and an asset that often commands a premium with investors. A large room or primary-suite addition, by contrast, rarely produces direct income but can significantly improve your living comfort and resale appeal. It may be simpler to finance via standard home improvement loans and can avoid some of the privacy and parking challenges that come with a rental unit. To compare ROI, model a 10-year horizon: net rental income after expenses for the ADU versus estimated resale value increase and personal value from the addition. Discuss both scenarios with a local real estate professional and a contractor who can provide realistic cost ranges, then weigh financial returns against lifestyle priorities and management appetite.
acceptedAnswer.description: Compare total project cost, rentable square footage, expected rent, and property tax impact for an ADU against the added resale value and lifestyle benefits of a room addition. An ADU may generate cash flow and rental flexibility, while an addition can better serve your own space needs and simplify financing and management.
